evidence: Hang Bo Street, nestled amidst the intricate network of the Old Quarter, is a bustling highlight that bears the strong imprint of trade in the thousand-year-old capital of civilization. This charming street, known as Phố Hàng Bồ in Vietnamese, has a rich history dating back to centuries past, when it was a gathering place for weavers specializing in making and selling large baskets, hampers, and rattan/bamboo trays for storing agricultural products.

As you wander down Hang Bo Street, you are surrounded by the vibrant colors of countless rolls of ribbon and lace, blended with the yellowish, moss-covered hues on the walls. The street's architecture is characterized by tube houses with sloping tiled roofs, which seem to lean in, as if sharing secrets with each other.
